authority_statement: Crew Chief is advisory; Maverick retains final authority.

findings.action: Replace in-place shared-to-exclusive lock conversion with an exclusive connection acquired from the outset, or make failed conversion explicitly reacquire and verify the prior shared lock before returning control. Add a multiprocess regression where two shared connections attempt maintenance concurrently and verify neither continues without a lock.
findings.blocking_rationale: This medium-severity concurrency defect is blocking because maintenance and migration safety depend on continuous exclusive ownership; a failed non-atomic flock conversion can leave an ordinary connection continuing without its recorded shared lock.

evidence.detail: Maintenance upgrades the lock attached to an already-open shared connection and restores the previous mode only after successful context entry.
The conversion repeatedly invokes non-blocking flock conversion but updates the recorded mode only after success; timeout handling does not explicitly reacquire or verify the prior lock.

findings.why_it_matters: BSD flock upgrades are not guaranteed to preserve the existing shared lock while attempting conversion. If two readers upgrade concurrently or an upgrade times out, the connection may remain open while its object still reports shared mode even though kernel lock ownership was lost. That breaks the full-connection locking invariant and can admit writes or maintenance during migration-sensitive work.
